brief.goal: A fast inference path for the L+2 learned block heads T0 and T3 that has the serving scorer's shape. It takes the inputs serving already holds on the device: the biased fp32 target-gate scores, bf16 x and the source layer's routes and route weights. It produces the same cap-1 read the frozen F109 reference would make. Alongside it: - a measured per-component cost breakdown and the incremental cost over the native score+select kernels, under CUDA graphs at live widths 1-6; - a side-stream interference measurement; - read-set parity against the frozen F109 thresholds on every dev and calib group. Nothing is wired into serving. That is Stage 3.
criteria: Profile of today's reference path (r1_cost's complete path) for T0 and T3 at six tokens under a CUDA graph. It gives separate medians for gate, feature build (PCA plus E5), head MLP, block aggregation plus sigmoid, and mask-threshold-select, with the graph node count of each component.
A folded torch implementation (`fast_head_torch`) of T0 and T3, mathematically equal to the reference:
it consumes precomputed gate scores;
the PCA mean is folded into the first-layer biases;
the sparse E5 inputs (route mask, route weights, top-12 scores and margins) are applied as column gathers, not dense [tokens, 384] scatters;
the source/target/stratum embedding contributions are precomputed into one per-(source, target) bias;
its block scores match the reference's to |diff| <= 1e-4 (fp32) on real groups.
Fused JIT CUDA kernels (`spec_head`) implementing the same computation in at most four launches after the native score kernel, on the same stream:
(1) PCA projection plus `fc_in`;
(2) the residual/gated middle block;
(3) `fc_out`;

(4) a fused tail: T0's noisy-or or T3's block aggregator MLP, then sigmoid, hot/RAM skip masks, threshold and cap-1 argmax. The kernels output the selected expert and its score in the serving candidate-record convention: count 0 or 1, and the block score in the margin field.

Parity on every dev and calib group (44,536 + 20,254) for T0 and T3, at the F109 frozen calib threshold (budget 0.75) and at budget 1.0. For both the folded torch path and the fused kernels it reports:
block-score max/p99 |diff|;
top-1 agreement;
read-set agreement (same read, or same abstention);
every disagreement within 1e-3 of the threshold, listed separately. Ties, padding (width < 6), all-skipped rows and the hot/RAM masks each have a unit test.
Parity is checked twice:
with the reference's own fp32 gate scores;

with scores produced by the serving `spec_score` kernel from the same x, using the live gate-weight dtype. Any read-set difference in the second case is reported as a precision candidate with its recall change at the frozen threshold. It is not hidden.
Cost under a CUDA graph at live widths 1, 2, 4 and 6 (RTX 5090), all medians of at least 1000 replays:
native `spec_score` plus `spec_select` alone;
native score plus the fused learned path plus its select;
the folded torch path;
the incremental cost over native, for T0 and T3. The historical 0.1 ms/layer bar is reported beside each number.

Side-stream interference: the fused learned path is replayed on a side stream while a fixed main-stream load runs (bf16 GEMMs sized like one decode layer's dense work). The report gives the main-stream slowdown against the native scorer on the same side stream, and against no side work.

`REPORT.md` and `result.json` in a new `/mnt/nvme1` directory hold all of the above, with commands, checkpoint hashes, the measurement scope beside every number, and the labels "observed offline" / "hypothesis". The results are recorded as DSV41_REFERENCE §33.31.
rules: R1: Never write into the R1, R2, F108 or F109 run directories. Outputs go to a new directory under /mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/.
R2: Never open the locked test split.
R3: Do not change serving behaviour, any launch flag, env var default or production default. Existing JIT kernels and their wrappers keep byte-identical behaviour.
R4: Verify checkpoint sha256s on load (T0 e6f7661d..., T3 e675e2bd...) and record them.
R5: divix01 protocol:
R6: pushed commits, private wt-* worktree, PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python, print sglang.__file__;
R7: CPU work under taskset -c 0-63 with OMP_NUM_THREADS;
R8: GPU work under flock cc-gpu.lock taskset -c 32-63;
R9: run only affected tests, through divix01-pytest (with --gpu for kernel tests);
R10: production untouched.

Module layout (D6): flat modules analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/l2_fast_<part>.py, each with a sibling test_l2_fast_<part>.py in the same directory (not under test/registered). Copy the R1 header from r1_cost.py / l2_cap1_scorers.py: a docstring giving purpose, inputs, output and usage; HERE/REPO; sys.path.insert of scripts/dsv41, analysis/dsv41-drive/router-capture and HERE; then `import r1_x  # noqa: E402`. Tests do `sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))` and build small synthetic R1Models the way test_l2_cap1_cost.py::_model does (HeadConfig variant='E5', PCAStats over X_DIM=5120, Vocab, R1Config(position=..., aggregator=...)). Use a nonzero PCA mean and nonzero embeddings so the folds are actually exercised.

Reuse the reference; don't fork it. The reference is r1_models.R1Model, run through its forward on ModelInput built like r1_cost._gate_features / r1_cache.collate. Gate scores come from r1_gate.full_gate_scores / load_target_gates. Selection uses r1_cost.select_torch and r1_policy.candidates/select (skipped rows never read; ties to the lowest expert id). T3 features come from r1_aggregator.block_features. Checkpoints load through r1_models.load_r1 and are verified with l2_cap1_scorers.learned_ckpts + verify_ckpt. Groups load as l2_cap1_eval does: read_r1_groups(horizon=2) with R1 exclusions, then l2_cap1_scorers.split_covered. x comes from r1_cache.make_x_of. Graph timing reuses r1_cost._capture / _time_graph and b1_cost._replay_times_ms.
Existing r1_*, b1_*, l2_cap1_* modules and their tests are read-only for this feature. Import their helpers, private ones included, rather than editing them.

Kernel file: python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/expert_stream/spec_head.cuh follows spec_score.cuh's style. Use a `__grid_constant__` params struct per kernel and a host launcher struct `SpecHeadKernel` with static methods. Check inputs with expert_stream::verify_named + TensorMatcher/SymbolicSize + RuntimeCheck (tensor_checks.h). Launch with LaunchKernel on the tensors' device stream, no PDL. Doxygen \brief/\param on exported entities. Reuse device::expert_stream::{ranks_above, neg_inf, kScoreTokenTile} and wire::SpecCandidates offsets by #include. Write the output record as count (0 or 1) at kCandCount, expert at kCandExpert and block score at kCandMargin, into a device or pinned buffer the caller passes.

Never edit spec_score.cuh, spec_candidates.h, exl3_ram_miss.cuh, or expert_stream_transport.py's _device_wrappers / _SPEC_METHODS / _device_module*. spec_head is its own JIT module: `@cache_once` + `load_jit("expert_stream_spec_head", cuda_files=["moe/expert_stream/spec_head.cuh"], cuda_wrappers=[(..., "SpecHeadKernel::<method>")])`. Its Python wrapper goes in a new module python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/spec_head.py, beside expert_stream_transport.py, which is already over 3k lines. The wrapper takes the same skip inputs as run_spec_select (hot_slots, hot_capacity, ram_slot, target). Nothing under python/sglang/srt imports it.

Kernel/folded contract: weights are stored bf16 and activations fp32 between launches (D3). Inputs are spec_scores fp32 [tokens_max, 384], x bf16 [tokens, 5120], source route ids int64 [tokens, top_k] and route weights fp32 [tokens, top_k], width, and the target row index into the precomputed per-row bias table (D4). The kernels take scores, never the gate weight (D2).

Python style (.claude/rules): msgspec.Struct, never @dataclass (FoldedHead is a msgspec.Struct). Call by keyword. Pure functions under ~100 LOC, files under ~2k LOC. A pseudocode-like orchestration function. Protected _helpers. No defensive getattr/hasattr. Comments only for facts the code can't show: ASCII, one or two lines.

Tests follow .claude/rules/unit-test-admission.md: each case names the regression it catches. GPU tests go in test/manual/dsv41/test_exl3_spec_head_cuda.py, or in analysis tests that need CUDA, with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), ...)`, and run through divix01-pytest --gpu. test/manual/dsv41/test_exl3_ram_prefetch_gpu_scorer_cuda.py stays unedited and green.

Checks: pytest only through `/Users/dnikolaidis/.hx/checks/divix01-pytest <named files> -q -p no:randomly` (`--gpu ... -q -s -p no:randomly` for CUDA), naming files, never a directory. On the laptop only `python3 -m py_compile <files>`. Never uv run, uv sync, pip install or .venv paths, and never commit python/uv.lock or python/.python-version. A new JIT module cold-builds on its first run; that is slow, not a failure.

Output safety: every CLI resolves --out with r1_stage.guard_out_root(root='/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work', forbidden=(b1-run-20261012, b1-r1-20261012, b1-r2-20261012, l2-ab-20261012, the F108 dirs, f109-l2-cap1-20261013)) and refuses paths inside RUN_DIR, as l2_cap1_eval.guard_out does. Write every file atomically (tmp + os.replace). The default OUT is /mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/f123-l2-fast-<date>.
Frozen thresholds are read from f109-l2-cap1-20261013/result.json (calib, budgets 0.75 and 1.0, per scorer L2_T0 / L2_T3), read only, and never refit (D7).

Labels and reporting: every number in result.json and REPORT.md carries its measurement scope (widths, replays, graph or eager, stream, L2-defeating rotation) and the label 'observed offline' or 'hypothesis'. Any number a run has not yet produced is written `pending`. DSV41_REFERENCE.md gets a new §33.31 appended after §33.30, with nothing else in that file changed.

The real divix01 run (profile, cost, interference, parity on all groups) is l2_fast_run.sh, an owner-started final task, never a batch check. It copies l2_cap1_run.sh: refuse dsv41-direct-prod, guard OUT, record git_head and sglang.__file__, and log each command through `_logged` (CMD/EXIT lines to commands.txt), with GPU steps under flock cc-gpu.lock taskset -c 32-63.

### Reference profile
`l2_fast_profile.py` wraps r1_cost's complete path. It captures each component as its own CUDA graph at six tokens,
times it, and counts graph nodes through `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` debug or nsys-free node counts. It writes

# Stage 2: a serving-shaped fast path for the L+2 learned heads (T0, T3), with cost and parity

## Goal
A fast inference path for the L+2 learned block heads T0 and T3 that has the serving scorer's shape. It takes the
inputs serving already holds on the device: the biased fp32 target-gate scores, bf16 x and the source layer's routes
and route weights. It produces the same cap-1 read the frozen F109 reference would make. Alongside it:
- a measured per-component cost breakdown and the incremental cost over the native score+select kernels, under CUDA
  graphs at live widths 1-6;
- a side-stream interference measurement;
- read-set parity against the frozen F109 thresholds on every dev and calib group.
Nothing is wired into serving. That is Stage 3.

## Acceptance criteria
- Profile of today's reference path (r1_cost's complete path) for T0 and T3 at six tokens under a CUDA graph. It gives
  separate medians for gate, feature build (PCA plus E5), head MLP, block aggregation plus sigmoid, and
  mask-threshold-select, with the graph node count of each component.
- A folded torch implementation (`fast_head_torch`) of T0 and T3, mathematically equal to the reference:
  - it consumes precomputed gate scores;
  - the PCA mean is folded into the first-layer biases;
  - the sparse E5 inputs (route mask, route weights, top-12 scores and margins) are applied as column gathers, not
    dense [tokens, 384] scatters;
  - the source/target/stratum embedding contributions are precomputed into one per-(source, target) bias;
  - its block scores match the reference's to |diff| <= 1e-4 (fp32) on real groups.
- Fused JIT CUDA kernels (`spec_head`) implementing the same computation in at most four launches after the native
  score kernel, on the same stream:
  - (1) PCA projection plus `fc_in`;
  - (2) the residual/gated middle block;
  - (3) `fc_out`;
  - (4) a fused tail: T0's noisy-or or T3's block aggregator MLP, then sigmoid, hot/RAM skip masks, threshold and
    cap-1 argmax.
  The kernels output the selected expert and its score in the serving candidate-record convention: count 0 or 1, and
  the block score in the margin field.
- Parity on every dev and calib group (44,536 + 20,254) for T0 and T3, at the F109 frozen calib threshold (budget
  0.75) and at budget 1.0. For both the folded torch path and the fused kernels it reports:
  - block-score max/p99 |diff|;
  - top-1 agreement;
  - read-set agreement (same read, or same abstention);
  - every disagreement within 1e-3 of the threshold, listed separately.
  Ties, padding (width < 6), all-skipped rows and the hot/RAM masks each have a unit test.
- Parity is checked twice:
  - with the reference's own fp32 gate scores;
  - with scores produced by the serving `spec_score` kernel from the same x, using the live gate-weight dtype.
  Any read-set difference in the second case is reported as a precision candidate with its recall change at the
  frozen threshold. It is not hidden.
- Cost under a CUDA graph at live widths 1, 2, 4 and 6 (RTX 5090), all medians of at least 1000 replays:
  - native `spec_score` plus `spec_select` alone;
  - native score plus the fused learned path plus its select;
  - the folded torch path;
  - the incremental cost over native, for T0 and T3.
  The historical 0.1 ms/layer bar is reported beside each number.
- Side-stream interference: the fused learned path is replayed on a side stream while a fixed main-stream load runs
  (bf16 GEMMs sized like one decode layer's dense work). The report gives the main-stream slowdown against the native
  scorer on the same side stream, and against no side work.
- `REPORT.md` and `result.json` in a new `/mnt/nvme1` directory hold all of the above, with commands, checkpoint
  hashes, the measurement scope beside every number, and the labels "observed offline" / "hypothesis". The results are
  recorded as DSV41_REFERENCE §33.31.

## Decisions
- Both T0 and T3 get the fast path. The choice between them is made after both are measured, from accuracy (F109)
  against incremental cost. Neither is assumed to win.
- The learned path reuses serving's `spec_scores` (biased fp32 [tokens, 384]) instead of recomputing the gate. The
  offline reference recomputes it in fp32 from the checkpoint's gate weight. The difference is measured by the second
  parity case, not assumed away.
- Weights: bf16 storage, fp32 accumulation and fp32 activations between kernels. This is the precision of R1's bf16
  cost path, so any read-set change it causes counts as a precision candidate, per the parity criterion.
- The per-(source, target) embedding bias is precomputed at load time from the checkpoint, for the 38 serving rows at
  horizon 2. The stratum is fixed per target row, as in the dataset.
- The kernels live with the expert-stream JIT kernels (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/expert_stream/spec_head.cuh`
  plus a Python wrapper beside the `SpecScoreKernel` wrappers). They are callable from offline harnesses and are not
  referenced by any serving code path, launch flag or default.
- Offline harness code lives in `analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/` as new `l2_fast_*.py` modules, with sibling
  tests, following R1's module layout.
- No training, retraining or recalibration. If the fast path changes reads, the change is reported. The threshold is
  never refit to hide it.
- Autonomous run: the owner told the session to proceed autonomously, so this spec is self-approved.

## Rules
- Never write into the R1, R2, F108 or F109 run directories. Outputs go to a new directory under
  `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/`.
- Never open the locked test split.
- Do not change serving behaviour, any launch flag, env var default or production default. Existing JIT kernels and
  their wrappers keep byte-identical behaviour.
- Verify checkpoint sha256s on load (T0 e6f7661d..., T3 e675e2bd...) and record them.
- divix01 protocol:
  - pushed commits, private `wt-*` worktree, `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python`, print `sglang.__file__`;
  - CPU work under `taskset -c 0-63` with `OMP_NUM_THREADS`;
  - GPU work under `flock cc-gpu.lock taskset -c 32-63`;
  - run only affected tests, through `divix01-pytest` (with `--gpu` for kernel tests);
  - production untouched.
- Size microbenchmarks honestly: weights are per-layer-shared, but the gate scores and x must be fresh per replay
  across at least 38 layer slots, so the measurement does not sit in L2.

## Non-goals
- Serving integration, a launch flag or a served A/B (Stage 3).
- Training a cheaper student or a gate-anchored correction.
- Changing model capacity.
- The F108 reverse order, native margin floors, L+4.

  gathers and the bias.
- K2 is the 512x512 r1/r2 and 128x512 gate block.
- K3 is `fc_out` 512->384.
- K4 is one block over 384 experts: the tail (noisy-or, or the T3 aggregator features plus the 42->32->1 MLP),
  sigmoid, skip masks, threshold and argmax.
The wrapper `SpecHeadKernel` sits beside `SpecScoreKernel` and takes the same skip inputs as `spec_select`.

### Parity harness

reference R1GroupScorer, the folded path and the kernels on the same inputs. It applies the F109 frozen thresholds

### Cost and interference

## Testing
- CPU and GPU unit tests on synthetic weights and groups:
  - the folded path equals an unfolded reimplementation;
  - the kernels equal the folded path (scores to 1e-3, identical cap-1 picks away from ties);

tasks.title: l2_fast_torch: fold T0/T3 into a FoldedHead and score from precomputed gate scores
tasks.intent:
Implement the folded torch path (C2-C7): an exact refactoring of r1_models.R1Model for T0 (noisy-or) and T3 (position + BlockAggregator). It takes biased fp32 gate scores, x, source routes and the row, and returns the [384] block score.

**Steps:**
- New `l2_fast_torch.py` with the R1 header.
- `class FoldRow(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True)` with source_layer, target_layer (layer ids) and stratum (str).
- `serving_rows(groups) -> tuple[FoldRow, ...]` gives the unique (source, target, stratum) triples of R1Groups, sorted by target. It raises if one target has two sources or strata (D4).
- `fold(model, *, rows, dtype=torch.float32) -> FoldedHead` (a frozen msgspec.Struct of tensors). It refuses cfg.adapter_rank > 0 and variant != 'E5'; T0/T3 have neither (r1_plan arms). Fields:
  - `w_pca` = pca_components [128, 5120].
  - `w_in_pca` = fc_in's PCA columns [512, 128].
  - `b_in` = fc_in.bias - w_in_pca @ (P @ mu). `b_gate` = fc_gate.bias - fc_gate.weight @ (P @ mu) (C4).
  - `w_in_sparse` [4, 384, 512]: fc_in's mask, route, gate-score and margin column blocks, transposed so one expert is one contiguous row (C5).
  - `row_bias` [R, 512] = fc_in's embedding columns @ cat(source_emb, target_emb, stratum_emb) of each row, using vocab indices (C6, D4).
  - `pos_bias` [6 widths, 6 positions, 512] = pos_proj(cat(pos_emb(p), w/6)) for T3, or an empty tensor.
  - The r1, r2, gate and out weights and biases.
  - For T3: `agg_w1` = mlp[0].weight[:, :10] [32, 10]; `agg_row_bias` [R, 32] = mlp[0].bias + mlp[0].weight[:, 10:] @ cat(layer_emb(target), stratum_emb(stratum)); `agg_w2` [32]; `agg_b2` [1]. Empty tensors for T0.
  - `rows`.
- `row_index(folded, *, target_layer) -> int`.
- `score(folded, *, scores, x, src_ids, src_w, positions, row) -> Tensor`. Tokens = x.shape[0] (1..6); only scores[:tokens] are used. It returns fp32 sigmoid(block logit) [384]. Per token:
  - h = x @ w_pca.T.
  - pre = w_in_pca h + b_in + row_bias[row] (+ pos_bias[tokens-1, pos]).
  - Add gathered rows of w_in_sparse: mask 1 and route weight for src_ids; gate score and margin (score minus the 6th-best, b1_rows.TOPK) for the top-12 (b1_rows.GATE_DEPTH) of `scores`, ordered by (higher score, lower id).
  - v = gelu(pre); r = r2(gelu(r1 v)); g = sigmoid(w_gate h + b_gate); logits = w_out (v + g r) + b_out.
  - Block: T0 = r1_models._noisy_or_logit over live tokens; T3 = r1_aggregator.block_features(..., position=positions), then agg_w1 @ feats + agg_row_bias[row] -> gelu -> agg_w2 + agg_b2.
  - It must be graph-capturable: no host syncs, static shapes for a given token count.
- `select_cap1(block_scores, *, skip, threshold) -> (count int32[1], expert int64[1], value fp32[1])` takes the best non-skipped score >= threshold, ties to the lowest id, and gives expert -1 / count 0 otherwise. It is graph-capturable (reuse r1_cost.select_torch with cap=1).

**Asserts** (sibling `test_l2_fast_torch.py`, CPU, synthetic models built like test_l2_cap1_cost.py::_model, with a nonzero PCA mean and embeddings):
- For T0-like (aggregator off) and T3-like (position + aggregator) models, `score` equals torch.sigmoid(R1Model(ModelInput)) to 1e-5. The ModelInput's u is built as r1_cost._gate_features does, and the scores come from r1_gate.full_gate_scores.
- That holds at widths 1 and 6 and with non-contiguous positions.
- fold refuses an adapter.
- select_cap1 ties go to the lowest id; all skipped gives count 0; a threshold above every score gives count 0; and it agrees with r1_policy.candidates + select(cap=1).

**Verify:** `python3 -m py_compile analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/l2_fast_torch.py analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/test_l2_fast_torch.py` prints nothing.

**Never:** densify E5 into [tokens, 384] scatters inside `score`; recompute the gate from W inside the path (D2); edit r1_*/b1_* modules.

tasks.title: spec_head_tail.cuh: K4 fused tail (noisy-or or aggregator, sigmoid, skips, threshold, cap-1 argmax)
tasks.intent:
Write kernel K4 (C12) as its own header that spec_head.cuh includes. Given the token logits it computes the block score per expert and publishes one cap-1 pick in the serving candidate-record convention.

**Steps:**
- New `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/expert_stream/spec_head_tail.cuh` in spec_score.cuh's style. Include `spec_score.cuh` for `device::expert_stream::{ranks_above, neg_inf}` and `spec_candidates.h` for `wire::SpecCandidates`.
- Constants in `device::expert_stream`: kHeadMaxExperts=384, kHeadTailThreads=384, kHeadMaxTokens=8, kBlockFeatures=10, kAggHidden=32.
- `struct SpecHeadTailParams { const float* logits /*[tokens, experts]*/; const int64_t* positions /*[tokens]*/; int64_t tokens; int64_t experts; const bf16_t* agg_w1 /*[kAggHidden,kBlockFeatures] or nullptr = noisy-or*/; const float* agg_bias /*the row's [kAggHidden]*/; const bf16_t* agg_w2 /*[kAggHidden]*/; const float* agg_b2 /*[1]*/; const int64_t* hot_slots; int64_t hot_capacity; const int32_t* ram_slot /*target row, >=0 mapped*/; const float* threshold /*[1]*/; float* block_scores /*[experts]*/; float* features /*[experts,kBlockFeatures] or nullptr*/; uint8_t* record /*kCandStride bytes*/; };`
- `__global__ __launch_bounds__(kHeadTailThreads, 1) void spec_head_tail_kernel(const __grid_constant__ SpecHeadTailParams p)`: one block, one thread per expert.
  - T0: noisy-or logit s + log(-expm1(-s)), with s = sum of softplus over tokens clamped to r1_models._TINY. Use torch's softplus threshold of 20.
  - T3: the 10 features in r1_aggregator.block_features order (anchor = position 0; draft max; peak; mean; population std; sum; noisy-or prob; count), then agg_w1 -> + agg_bias -> exact-erf GELU -> agg_w2 + agg_b2.
  - block = sigmoid(logit), written to block_scores for every expert.
  - Skip = ram_slot[e] >= 0, or e in hot_slots[:hot_capacity], exactly as exl3_ram_prefetch_select_kernel builds it.
  - Block argmax over non-skipped experts with score >= *threshold, by ranks_above (ties to the lower id).
  - Record: u32 at kCandCount = count (0 or 1), flags 0. When count is 1, entry 0 is expert | rank 0 << 16 at kCandEntries + kCandExpert, and the f32 block score at kCandEntries + kCandMargin. The u32 seq = 1 at kCandSeq is stored last, after a __threadfence. When count is 0, entry 0's expert is written as 0xFFFF.
- Doxygen \brief on the params and kernel.

**Guards:** experts <= kHeadMaxExperts and 1 <= tokens <= kHeadMaxTokens (the launcher checks; the kernel assumes). NaN logits rank below all, as spec_score does.

**Never:** edit spec_score.cuh, spec_candidates.h or exl3_ram_miss.cuh (R3).

tasks.intent:
Write the fused head body (C8-C11) and the host launcher `SpecHeadKernel`. `run` issues at most four launches (K1, K2, K3, then T3's K4) on the tensors' stream, after the native score kernel; `tail` issues K4 alone.

**Steps:**
- New `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/expert_stream/spec_head.cuh`. It #includes `spec_head_tail.cuh` (T3's contract) and `tensor_checks.h`. Style follows spec_score.cuh: `__grid_constant__` params structs, fp32 accumulation with bf16 weights (D3), and fp32 workspaces between launches.
- K1: a tiled GEMV of bf16 x [T,5120] against w_pca [128,5120], sharing kScoreTokenTile=8, into h [8,128].
  - Per token, the top-12 of `scores` row t by ranks_above. Its margin is score minus the 6th-best (b1_rows.TOPK = 6, GATE_DEPTH = 12).
